name: Spastic Paraplegia-Neuropathy-Poikiloderma Syndrome
aliases: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia with Poikiloderma and Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Distal sensory-motor peripheral neuropathy confirmed by clinical and electrophysiological studies
Presence of poikiloderma characterized by skin atrophy, telangiectasia, and pigmentation abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the CTC1 gene or related loci

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progressive spastic paraplegia, sensory-motor neuropathy, and poikiloderma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by genetic testing where available

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
Normal routine blood counts and metabolic panels
imaging: MRI brain may show mild cerebral or cerebellar atrophy
Spinal cord MRI typically normal or shows mild atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CTC1 gene associated with telomere maintenance defects
other: Electrophysiological studies showing axonal sensory-motor neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily pure spastic paraplegia phenotype without neuropathy
Severe photosensitivity with early skin cancers
Neurological symptoms less prominent or absent

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity and weakness
Early onset of poikiloderma with neurological symptoms
Family history suggestive of autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Recent clinical case series and reviews on SPNP syndrome (2023)
